name: Geroch monotonicity / Huisken-Ilmanen: Hawking mass non-decreasing under inverse mean curvature flow when R >= 0; proof of the Riemannian Penrose inequality

source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0906.5566, 2210.12237, 2605.00680 (pages listed above). Geroch 1973, Jang-Wald 1977 and Huisken-Ilmanen 2001 themselves: NAMED-NOT-READ. In particular HI's own statement of the weak monotonicity formula (their 'Geroch Monotonicity Formula', sec.5) and their exact connectedness lemma (sec.4) were NOT read here; their content is taken only as Mars restates it.

published_statement: Mars 0906.5566 p.21 (sec.5.3): 'the Geroch mass (17) (with C = 0) is monotonically increasing if the surfaces are moved by inverse mean curvature (i.e. p e^psi = 1) provided the scalar curvature of (Sigma, gamma) is non-negative. This fact is clear from (18) ... Another immediate property of M_G is that its value on any connected, topologically S^2 minimal surface is M_G = sqrt(|S|/(16 pi)). For surfaces S_r ... in the asymptotically euclidean end ... lim M_G(S_r) = M_ADM.' Definition (17): M_G(S) = sqrt(|S|/16pi)(chi(S)/2 - (1/16pi) int_S (p^2 + 4C/3)); 'Hence chi(S) = 2 for a connected surface with spherical topology' (p.10); Geroch mass = Hawking mass 'when the surface is embedded in a time-symmetric initial data set' (p.10), and M_G <= M_H in general (p.11). Weak flow (p.21-22): level-set IMCF div(grad u/|grad u|) = |grad u| (35), weak solutions via J_u(v) = int(|grad v| + v|grad u|) (36), leaves outer-area-minimizing, jumps across which 'the Geroch mass is non-decreasing provided the Euler characteristic of the surface does not decrease'; 'The example with two spheres in Euclidean space shows that this cannot be true in general'; HI: 'a topologically S^2 surface in an asymptotically euclidean three-manifold outside the outermost minimal surface cannot jump ... to another surface with smaller Euler characteristic'; 'Consequently ... a connected component S_i of the outermost minimal surface must be chosen as initial surface. The Penrose inequality proven by Huisken and Ilmanen is, therefore, M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi) (37)', with rigidity: equality iff the exterior is isometric to Schwarzschild r > m/2. Hirsch 2210.12237 p.1: 'Huisken and T. Ilmanen proved the Riemannian Penrose inequality for connected horizons'; p.3: for (M,g) 'asymptotically flat, 3-dimensional, complete ... with non-negative scalar curvature R', 'The famous monotonicity formula for the Hawking mass under IMCF [19, 32, 29] states that d_t m_H(Sigma_t) >= 0 where m_H(Sigma) = sqrt(|Sigma|/16pi)(1 - (1/16pi) int H^2)'; eq.(6): m_H(Sigma_t) - m_H(Sigma_0) = (1/16pi) int_{Omega_t} (R|grad u| + ...) dV, RHS non-negative when R >= 0.
published_hypotheses: (Riemannian setting) a 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold (Sigma, gamma) -- in GR a TIME-SYMMETRIC initial data set (second fundamental form k = 0), where Geroch mass = Hawking mass (Mars p.10-11)
scalar curvature R(gamma) >= 0 (equivalently, for time-symmetric data, local energy density >= 0)
the flowing surface CONNECTED (Euler characteristic chi(S_t) <= 2; the Hawking-mass normalisation with '1' presumes chi = 2) -- Mars p.10 eq.(13)/(17) and p.22; Hirsch p.1 'connected horizons'

smooth IMCF with H > 0 (Geroch/Jang-Wald, heuristic: smooth flow generically develops singularities, Mars p.3, p.21) OR the Huisken-Ilmanen weak (level-set, outer-area-minimising) flow, for which monotonicity needs that the Euler characteristic not decrease across jumps -- guaranteed by HI for an S^2 leaf outside the outermost minimal surface in an asymptotically euclidean 3-manifold (Mars p.22)

for the Riemannian Penrose inequality and m_H -> M_ADM: (M,g) complete, asymptotically flat/euclidean, and the initial surface a connected component of the outermost minimal surface; the inequality proven is M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi), not the sum over components (Mars eq.(37)); the full (sum/area of all components) Riemannian inequality is Bray 2001 by a different (conformal) flow; the general non-time-symmetric Penrose inequality remains open (Mars; Hirsch p.1, p.12 'wide open outside spherical symmetry')
dimension 3 (Gauss-Bonnet is what cancels the constant term)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- connectedness / chi <= 2 of the flowing surface. overturn.py:138-140 states 'm_H IS monotone non-decreasing under inverse mean curvature flow when the scalar curvature R >= 0' with R >= 0 as the only hypothesis. Shown false without it: two disjoint unit spheres in flat R^3 (R = 0) under IMCF have m_H = -sqrt(e^t/2), strictly decreasing (rederive D1, D2; Mars p.22 names the same two-sphere example). Same drop at paper/CLAIMS.md:2640-2641 and CLAIMS.md:3109-3111. Does not move the tree's conclusion (L1 OPEN), see grade.

CLAIMS.md:3111 'carries it through singularities' is accurate as a gloss.

IMPLICIT (not drift, a named hypothesis to carry) -- time symmetry. overturn.py:134 writes m_H with only the Riemannian mean curvature H; that is the Geroch mass, equal to the Hawking mass only on time-symmetric data (Mars p.10-11). The tree's setting is STATIC spacetimes (overturn.py:128-131), whose Killing-orthogonal slice has k = 0, so the identification holds there; outside staticity (nonstatic.py's door) the spacetime Hawking mass with theta+ theta- (Hirsch p.1) is the object and its monotonicity has an existence theory only in spherical symmetry (Hirsch Thm 4.2).

WEAKENED (scope of 'proved the Riemannian Penrose inequality', overturn.py:140-141) -- HI's IMCF proof gives M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi) over connected components (connected horizon); the full Riemannian Penrose inequality for disconnected horizons is Bray 2001 (conformal flow), and all dimensions Bi-Zhu 2605.00680 (Bray-type flow). A gloss, not an error: the RPI in 3D is proved, and IMCF is one of the two proofs.

ADDED/INTERPRETIVE (not a hypothesis of the source) -- overturn.py:141-142 'It is the closest existing thing to requirement (b)' [controls proper distance]: the sources say nothing about proper distance; this is the tree's own judgement, correctly not attributed to the sources.

HAWKING-MASS REDUCTION (overturn.py:134-136, 'reduces to Misner-Sharp on round spheres'): holds -- rederive B2 shows m_H(round sphere) = m(r) exactly for dr^2/(1-2m/r) + r^2 dOmega^2, and B4 shows IMCF monotonicity there is exactly m'(r) >= 0 iff R >= 0. 'Not monotone in general': consistent with the sources (monotonicity is flow-specific).

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (15 checks, exit 0, ~2 min). A: symbolic algebra from the IMCF evolution equations + Gauss equation + Gauss-Bonnet gives dm_H/dt = sqrt(|N|/16pi)[(2-chi)/4 + (1/16pi) int(2|grad H|^2/H^2 + |A0|^2 + R)] -- the constant term vanishes iff chi = 2, so R >= 0 gives monotonicity for a connected sphere (and chi <= 2 keeps it >= 0). B: for dr^2/(1-2m(r)/r) + r^2 dOmega^2, R computed from Christoffels = 4m'/r^2, m_H(round sphere) = m(r) (Misner-Sharp), IMCF dr/dt = r/2, dm_H/dt = r^3 R/8, identical to A. C: non-round axisymmetric surface r = 1 + 0.15 P2(cos theta) in flat R^3: exact d/dt int H^2 under speed 1/H (moved surface differentiated symbolically, integrated at 30 digits) = -3.81235393977641677 equals the Geroch RHS to all printed digits; d|N|/dt = |N|; m_H = -0.0129 < 0 and dm_H/dt = +0.0318 > 0. D: two disjoint spheres (chi = 4, R = 0): m_H = -sqrt(e^t/2), dm_H/dt|_0 = -sqrt(2)/4 < 0, matching the formula's (2-chi)/4 = -1/2 term -- monotonicity fails without connectedness. E: Schwarzschild slice R = 0, m_H = M on every round sphere, horizon sqrt(|S|/16pi) = M saturates the RPI. Not checked here (not finite/closed-form): the HI weak-flow existence theory, the no-Euler-characteristic-drop-across-jumps lemma, and m_H -> M_ADM at infinity.

later_literature.what: Riemannian Penrose inequality for arbitrary (disconnected) outermost minimal surfaces via a conformal flow of metrics, using the positive mass theorem; closes the max_i gap left by IMCF.

Generalises Geroch's monotonicity to initial data sets with the dominant energy condition via a coupled PDE system for the spacetime Hawking mass (theta+ theta-); existence theory only for the a=0 system in general and the IMCF system in spherical symmetry (Thm 4.2); states the general Penrose conjecture 'wild open outside spherical symmetry' (p.12).

later_literature.ref: M. Mars, arXiv:0906.5566 (2009) sec.6 p.43, Weinstein-Yamada counterexample
later_literature.what: The charged Riemannian Penrose inequality (Jang, via IMCF, for connected S_m) fails when the outermost minimal surface has several components -- a worked instance that connectedness is load-bearing for IMCF-type results.
Riemannian Penrose inequality in all dimensions via Bray's conformal flow (not IMCF); restates HI as 'established the Geroch monotonicity for the Hawking mass along the weak flow' in dimension three.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The result is mathematics, not measurement, so no physical datum was missing and none has moved. What Geroch (1973) and Jang-Wald (1977) lacked was a MATHEMATICAL input: an existence theory for IMCF through singularities. Mars p.3 and p.21: 'The flow however, generically develops singularities and therefore the argument could not be made rigorous at the time'; two disjoint spheres must collide and a thin torus develops H = 0 on its inner rim. So their argument was INCOMPLETE exactly in M's sense -- and having the missing piece (HI 2001's weak level-set flow) did NOT change the conclusion; it confirmed it, with one narrowing: the jump analysis showed monotonicity requires the Euler characteristic not to drop, which forced HI to start from a CONNECTED component and prove M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi) rather than the full-area inequality (Mars eq.37), later completed by Bray by another method. Evidence against 'wrong': the monotonicity identity re-derives symbolically here (A), agrees with a direct exact computation on a non-round surface (C), and reproduces Misner-Sharp monotonicity in spherical symmetry (B). Evidence for 'incomplete as the tree quotes it': the tree's one-hypothesis statement (R >= 0 only) is refuted by the two-sphere example (D) -- the hypothesis was in the literature all along; the tree dropped it. For the tree's actual use (overturn L1, a quasi-local mass that controls proper distance outside spherical symmetry), no datum is relevant; the literature-state claim 'nobody has shown ... nobody has shown it cannot happen' (overturn.py:151-152) is a claim of absence that one discover_papers call cannot establish or refute -- it stays OPEN, as the tree grades it. One observation relevant to that framing, recorded not repaired: rederive C3 shows m_H < 0 on a non-round surface in FLAT space (Willmore: int H^2 >= 16 pi), so the sign of m_H off round spheres does not track matter sign; 'a surface with m_H(S) >= 0' (overturn.py:149-150) is therefore a stronger requirement than its spherical analogue.
grade_evidence: The published result STANDS as published: the Geroch monotonicity identity re-derives symbolically (A1-A3), matches an exact computation on a non-round surface in flat R^3 to 18 digits (C2), and reduces to Misner-Sharp monotonicity m' >= 0 <=> R >= 0 in spherical symmetry (B1-B4); Schwarzschild is the equality case (E1-E2). Two restating reviews (Mars 0906.5566, Hirsch 2210.12237) and a 2026 paper (Bi-Zhu 2605.00680) state HI's result consistently; no later work contradicts it. NARROWED because the tree's statement at overturn.py:138-140 (and paper/CLAIMS.md:2640-2641, 3109-3111) carries R >= 0 as the only hypothesis and drops connectedness of the flowing surface (chi <= 2), which the source requires; without it the statement is false -- two disjoint spheres in flat space, R = 0, have strictly decreasing m_H (D1-D2). It also drops the weak-flow setting (complete, asymptotically flat, start from a connected component of the outermost minimal surface) and overstates slightly that IMCF 'proved the Riemannian Penrose inequality': it proved M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi); the full statement is Bray 2001. Consequence for the tree: none on its verdict. overturn L1 is graded OPEN and uses Geroch/HI only as the nearest candidate tool, not as a premise; the narrowing (connected surfaces, time-symmetric = static slices) is compatible with the L1 programme as written, and the literature-absence claim at overturn.py:151-152 remains OPEN, not STANDS or WRONG.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restating the monotonicity with its connectedness hypothesis (connected leaves / chi <= 2; for the weak flow, start from a connected component of the outermost minimal surface in a complete asymptotically flat manifold) and 'proved the RPI for a connected horizon (Bray 2001 in general)'. To OPEN on the source side: nothing plausible -- but a direct read of HI 2001 sec.4-5 (not on arXiv; JDG 59, 353-437) could add hypotheses beyond those Mars restates (e.g. the exact topological condition in HI's connectedness lemma), which would lengthen the drift list, not reverse the grade. To WRONG: only a counterexample to HI's weak monotonicity under its own hypotheses, of which none is known in the literature read here.
